tools.name: npm_package
tools.description: Use when you need the public npm registry card for a package (scoped or unscoped): returns description, homepage, bugs URL, repository, license, keywords, maintainers as names only (emails stripped), number of versions, latest dist-tag version, created/modified times, and last-week download count fr

tools.name: npm_version
tools.description: Use when you need the exact published artifact for an npm version: dependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies, bundledDependencies, engines, os/cpu, dist (tarball URL, integrity, shasum, unpacked size), and the version publish time. Give "latest" as version to resolve the current dist-tag.

tools.name: npm_search
tools.description: Use to discover npm packages by keyword or name: returns up to 20 hits with name, version, description, keywords, date, and the registry search score. Publisher and maintainer emails are never returned (names/usernames only when present). Paid tool: x402 USDC on Base, $0.003 per successful call; cal

tools.name: pypi_project
tools.description: Use when you need the public PyPI project card: summary, home_page, project_urls, license, requires_python, a subset of classifiers, requires_dist (capped), current version, and yank status. Author/maintainer emails are omitted or redacted; only display names remain when present. Paid tool: x402 USD

tools.name: pypi_release
tools.description: Use when you need the published artifacts for a specific PyPI version: each file with filename, packagetype (sdist/bdist_wheel…), size, upload time, yank flags, digests (sha256/blake2b/md5) and download URL. Give "latest" as version to use the project's current version. Paid tool: x402 USDC on Base,

tools.name: pypi_search
tools.description: Use when you have a likely PyPI project name (or a few tokens) and need to resolve it to live projects: tries the query as-is, PEP 503 normalization (lowercase, [-_.] → -), and hyphen/underscore/dot variants, then returns up to "limit" matching projects with summary, version, requires_python and lic

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: npm_package, npm_version, npm_search, pypi_project, pypi_release, pypi_search · Private data: npm_package, pypi_release, pypi_search · Public sink: npm_version, pypi_release.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: npm_package, npm_version, npm_search, pypi_project, pypi_release, pypi_search · Private data: npm_package, pypi_release, pypi_search · Public sink: npm_version, pypi_release

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
